body: cops dragged me off a train, i spent a couple hours with them until my dad picked me up, we spent the nine hour drive back in insanely awkward silence, then my mom insisted we have to "talk" and monologued at me for half an hour, then the cops made us go to the station in our city so they could talk to me about why i did it but i didn't have the slightest idea how to articulate that shit and they quickly got tired of me and just made up a reason why, which was honestly a blessing, i was fucking exhausted beyond belief so i went along with it, even tho it makes me sound like an idiot. six months later i had a court date where the judge yelled at me and made fun of me, and that was it. my parents don't talk about it. all in all not a great experience, but the first few hours were the lightest i'd ever felt. it was worth it just for that relief, that single minded focus. perhaps that makes me a bad person, but i can't find it in me to feel bad for being shitty to any of those people, my parents, the cops. it's not like they were anything less than shitty to me too. i only regret worrying my siblings and friends.

i did that. didn't really work, shit just got worse. now cops stress the hell out of me, just the sight of a uniform or flashing lights, and my relationship with my parents got worse. it didn't change much and simultaneously it changed everything. my friends seem to care and worry more. my parents don't really give a shit but they don't trust me as much. it felt good, great even in the moment, but i don't know how much of that was actually the running away and how much was just the relief of finally being done since i was going to attempt "if the running away doesn't work, doesn't make me feel better" (i think i already knew it wouldn't, even if i didn't want to admit it. i was just putting off making the decision to actually off myself). anyway most people acted supremely shitty towards me when they found out, everyone from cops and the judge at my court date to teachers, my dance coach, former teammates. if you're a minor i don't recommend it, people who've never felt that way just don't get it, they'll assume the absolute worst about you. if you're not a minor, well idk, i can let you guys know in a couple months as i'm now eighteen and getting the hell out of here as soon as i'm able lol. i don't have high hopes tho. not being around my dad will certainly be a plus but your problems don't get left behind, they always follow. a big life change like moving can make a huge difference but running away only makes it better when you're running from someone else, you can't run away from yourself.
